answer.1: The center is a center of symmetry of both the sphere and the solid ball.
answer.2: Infinitely many axes and planes of symmetry: all lines and all planes through the center.

working: For center C and point M, central inversion gives M'=2C-M, so |M'-C|=|M-C|. This preserves both |M-C|=R (sphere, definition 1) and |M-C|<=R (solid ball, definition 2).
Rotation about any line through C and reflection in any plane through C preserve distance to C. Thus each such line is a symmetry axis and each such plane is a symmetry plane.
A symmetry must preserve the unique center, so no off-center line or plane adds a further axis or symmetry plane.
solutions.answerShape: Two subquestions, including a proof; the complete exercise must remain ungraded.

solutions.answer: A circle of radius R centered at the sphere center, lying in the given plane: a great circle, meaning the circumference rather than the filled disk.
working: Within a plane through C, the sphere condition |M-C|=R selects the circle circumference.
The filled disk would instead use |M-C|<=R and would be the section of the solid ball.
solutions.answerShape: A shape name with synonymous natural-language descriptions; ungraded is appropriate without reliable semantic text/shape judging.

solutions.condition: R>0, inherited from the sphere definition.
working: On the x-axis set y=z=0, giving x=+/-R; similarly for the y- and z-axes.
R>0 makes these six points distinct. They are a point set, not an ordered six-entry answer.
solutions.answerShape: Six unordered coordinate triples. Ungraded is appropriate if the runtime has no reliable unordered point-set judge; arbitrary order must not be made mathematically required.

working: A general point of the full line SO is (x,y,z)=(3t,4t,5t), t real.
Substitution gives (9+16+25)t^2=200, hence 50t^2=200, t=+/-2.
The t=2 point is (6,8,10), in the direction OS; t=-2 gives (-6,-8,-10).
Each point has squared norm 36+64+100=200. The line is not restricted to the positive ray.
solutions.answerShape: Two triples. Labeled positive and negative intersections allow six independently graded coordinates with fixed signs; no units.

working: The sphere has radius sqrt(p^2)=p. A is outside the sphere, so its distance to the surface is 7p-p=6p.
For any surface point M, |A-M|>=||A|-|M||=6p; equality is attained at M=A/7.
solutions.answerShape: One symbolic nonnegative distance, suitable for expression judging; p>0 cannot be dropped.

working: Use (x-a)^2+(y-b)^2+(z-c)^2=R^2, definition block 9.
Part 1: 2^2+(-1)^2+3^2=14 and R^2=16, so the constant in the zero form is 14-16=-2.
Part 2: (-5)^2+0^2+7^2=74 and R^2=(sqrt(3))^2=3, so the constant in the zero form is 74-3=71.
Completing the squares in each expanded form recovers the specified center and radius.
solutions.answerShape: Two independent complete equations, with equality signs and both sides. Compact and the listed expanded forms are mathematically equivalent; no length-unit suffix is given.
